summary: Kristin Scheible is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at Colby College and Harvard University under Anne E. Monius, Diana L. Eck, John S. Strong, and Charles Hallisey, she became Thomas Lamb Eliot Professor of Religion and Humanities at Reed College.

Kristina Myrvold works in religious studies and Indology. She studied at Lund University, where she was also an editor attested in 2005, and became Assistant Professor of Religious Studies at Linnaeus University, attested in 2014.

Kristofer Schipper (1934–2021) was a scholar of Sinology and religious studies who studied at the École du Louvre, INALCO, EPHE, and Paris Diderot University. He held posts at the EFEO, EPHE, Collège de France, Leiden University, and Fuzhou University.

Kristóf Szitár is a scholar in Iranian and Central Asian studies, religious studies, and Indology. Educated at Uppsala, CEU, Tübingen, and Lausanne, he held appointments at Lausanne, Heidelberg, Yale, the Institute of Ismaili Studies, and Yerevan State University.

Krisztina Teleki is a scholar of Tibetology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Eötvös Loránd University (~1996–2009) and later served there as a research fellow around 2010.
Kshanika Saha is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied under Nalinaksha Dutt and completed her PhD at the University of Calcutta (attested 1966).

Kshetresh Chandra Chattopadhyaya (1896–1974) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Ganganatha Jha and at the universities of Calcutta and Allahabad and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University. He taught at Allahabad from 1924 and directed the Sampurnanand Research Institute.

Kshitimohan Sen (1880–1960) was a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy who earned an M.A. at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University. He served in Chamba State (~1907–1908) and at Visva-Bharati University from 1908, becoming Adhyaksha in 1953–1954.

Kumataro Kawada (1899–1981) was a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who earned his doctorate at the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at Japan Women's University (1927), the University of Tokyo (1950–1959), and Komazawa University (1959).
Kumja Paik Kim is an art historian and Buddhist studies scholar who earned her doctorate at Stanford University. In 1989, she became curator of Korean art at the Asian Art Museum.

Kumkum Bandyopadhyay is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. Supervised by Rupendra Kumar Chattopadhyay, she has served as a research scholar and fellow at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026).

Kun Chang (1917–2017) was a linguist, Sinologist, and Tibetologist. He studied at Tsinghua and Yale under Franklin Edgerton and Geshe Nornang, working at Academia Sinica, the University of Washington from 1951, and UC Berkeley (1963–1987).

Kunio Harikai is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied at Kyushu University under Seiren Matsunami and Shōren Ihara, subsequently serving as associate professor at Saga University (~1976–1986) and Saga Medical School (~1986–1999).
Kunio Iwaya studied at the University of Tokyo from around 1961 to 1968. He later held an academic appointment at Meiji Gakuin University from approximately 1970 to 2014.
Kunio Mugitani is a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and philosophy who studied under Mitsuji Fukunaga (~1970–1976). He served as a professor at Kyoto University from around 1993 to 2012.
Kunio Odaka (1908–1993) studied at the University of Tokyo from around 1928 to 1931. He later held academic posts at the University of Tokyo (~1945–1969) and Sophia University (~1969–1979).

Kunio Yanagita (1875–1962) was a Japanologist and scholar of religious studies who studied law at the University of Tokyo. He worked for government ministries, the Tokyo Asahi Shimbun, and later taught at Keio and Kokugakuin universities.

Kuno Fischer (1824–1907) was a German philosopher who studied at the universities of Leipzig and Halle-Wittenberg. He held professorships at the University of Jena (~1856–1872) and Heidelberg University (~1872–1906).

Kuno Lorenz is a philosopher who studied at Tübingen, Hamburg, Bonn, Princeton, Kiel, and Erlangen-Nuremberg. He held the chair of philosophy at the University of Hamburg (1970) and was a professor at Saarland University (1974–1998).

Kuno Meyer (1858–1919) was a linguist who studied under Ernst Windisch at the University of Leipzig (~1879–1883). He held academic posts at the University of Liverpool (~1884–1911) and Frederick William University Berlin (~1911–1915).
